tldr: Ceuta crisis headlines read primarily as an EU border-hardening story: calls for 'united action' and stronger external borders dominate wire services, German, Nordic, and UK outlets, while a parallel POLITICAL stream frames the crisis as an intra-EU blame war—22 member states publicly attacking Spain. Militarised and invasionist language (barriers, troops, 'invaders', 'hybrid war', 'storm') runs through Chinese, US conservative, and Russian titles. Humanitarian costs and Morocco's causal role surface in a minority of headlines, and the Supreme Court legal trigger—central in body texts—is absent from every title.

paradox.joint_conclusion: RT and The Intercept headlines reach the same verdict — EU institutions failed on Ceuta — from opposite political poles: RT frames failure as collapse of a 'solidarity delusion' and celebrates EU fracture; The Intercept frames failure as liberal capitulation to far-right anti-migrant politics. Both conclusions are legible from the title alone, making this the rare headline-layer paradox that does not require body text to detect.

silences.note: Folha de São Paulo's sole headline ('Centenas de migrantes dormem em praia de Ceuta após travessia em massa') describes the beach encampment scene in Portuguese without committing to any policy, political, or moral frame — purely situational reporting that carries no frame signal.

Foreign Policy's headline ('Spain Records Unprecedented Migrant Crossing') is a bare factual label — no policy prescription, no political charge, no moral weight — despite the outlet's typical policy-analytical framing in body text.

The Spanish Supreme Court ruling banning summary 'hot returns' — identified in body text by CGTN World, BBC World, and others as the proximate legal trigger for the crossing — appears in zero of 49 headlines. The legal cause of the crisis is entirely invisible at homepage/RSS level, producing a systematic divergence between what readers learn from headlines versus bodies.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only headline in the 49-title corpus to use the term 'invaders' for migrants, absent even from Fox News and Daily Mail titles covering the same events.
single_outlet_findings.quote: Thousands Of Migrant Invaders Still Overwhelm Spanish City

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only headline to deploy 'hybrid war' framing and describe the crossings as a 'migrant attack on Spain,' treating migration as deliberate state-directed aggression — a register absent from all other outlets including conservative European press.
single_outlet_findings.quote: Hybrid war hypocrisy: How the migrant attack on Spain

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only headline to label Sánchez by party ('Socialist Spanish PM'), explicitly linking the border crisis to left-wing governance in the title — a partisan frame absent from other right-leaning outlets such as Daily Mail.
Only headline to critique liberal and centrist complicity in anti-migrant politics rather than the crisis itself, inverting the dominant security/political framing visible across all other outlets.
single_outlet_findings.quote: Liberals Are Ceding Ground to the Far Right on Ceuta

bottom_line: The headline layer of Ceuta coverage reads as an EU border-hardening and intra-bloc blame story: policy prescriptions for stronger borders and EU political fracture dominate, the human cost of 72+ deaths is a minority signal, and the legal trigger that body texts identify as proximate cause is invisible in every one of the 49 titles.
